references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the calling of the tax collector Matthew (Levi). Jesus sees him sitting at the tax booth and says "Follow me", just as in Luke's version.
Mark's parallel account of the calling of Levi, son of Alphaeus, who was sitting at the tax booth. Jesus says "Follow me" to him, which is a direct parallel to Luke 5:27.
The following verse tells of Levi's response: he left everything and followed Jesus. This immediate obedience is an important part of the calling narrative.
The calling of the first disciples, Peter and Andrew, by the Sea of Galilee. Jesus says "Follow me", and they leave everything to follow him – the same pattern as in Levi's calling.
Mark's account of the calling of Simon and Andrew, where Jesus invites them to follow him. The same call formula "Follow me" is used as in Levi's calling.
Peter, James, and John leave everything and follow Jesus after the miraculous catch of fish. The same theme of leaving all to follow Jesus as seen in Levi's calling.
Jesus finds Philip and says "Follow me." The same direct call that Jesus uses toward Levi at the tax booth.
Jesus says to the rich young man: "Sell everything you own ... and follow me." The same call, but here with a different outcome than in Levi's calling.

The account of the tax collector Zacchaeus. Jesus seeks out another tax collector, and Zacchaeus' repentance shows Jesus' care for tax collectors and sinners, which is also expressed in the calling of Levi.
